title: Factitious lymphoedema as a psychiatric condition mimicking reflex sympathetic dystrophy: a case report
case_prompt: A 33-year-old man presented with a 2-day history of severe burning pain in his left forearm. Twenty-two months earlier, he had sustained a left distal radius fracture treated by manipulation and plaster cast, which healed satisfactorily without neurovascular deficit. On examination, the forearm was discoloured, swollen, and intensely itchy; the hand was neurovascularly intact but had a reduced range of motion and limited function due to stiffness and pain. Physiotherapy with manipulative exercises and volar splints was initiated, but he continued to experience pain despite maximal opioid analgesia. He underwent a Bier’s sympathetic block, which relieved the pain transiently, but his symptoms and signs recurred shortly after discharge. On subsequent attendances, the distribution of the swelling and discolouration showed a clear line of demarcation at the mid-forearm, and the position of this line varied across consultations.
diagnostic_reasoning:
1. Initial suspicion of reflex sympathetic dystrophy was based on post-fracture presentation with burning pain, oedema, stiffness, and discolouration — “the patient was thought to have RSD because of his presentation and his previous distal radius fracture.”  
2. The absence of any known psychiatric history at presentation argued against an immediately suspected factitious cause — “The patient in this case did not have a known medical history of psychosis, behavioural disorder, self-harm or other psychiatric conditions that would have suggested that his presentation was FL not RSD.”  
3. External compression due to a ligature or proximal compress was considered when the swelling and discolouration showed a sharply demarcated line whose position varied — “the distribution of the swelling and discolouration of his forearm was more in keeping with the application of a ligature or proximal compress, resulting in subsequent swelling and discolouration.”  
4. Factitious lymphoedema was confirmed after psychiatric evaluation revealed self-induced intermittent tourniquet application — “This is a case of FL caused by intermittent application of a tourniquet to the forearm in a patient with an underlying psychiatric illness.”
